texts.title: Reconstruction of a Wednesday
texts.author: Manuel Academy
texts.source: Authored for Manuel Academy High School ELA; Academy-held rights.
texts.summary: A story told out of order whose events only cohere on re-reading; built for RL.5 structural analysis without an exemplar.
texts.opening_passage: The part everyone remembers is the part that happened last. This is inconvenient, because it is also the only part that makes no sense on its own.

texts.title: Two Reports, One River
texts.author: Manuel Academy
texts.source: Authored for Manuel Academy High School ELA; Academy-held rights.
texts.summary: A municipal report and a community newsletter describing the same water-quality event, differing in emphasis and omission.
texts.opening_passage: The Department's summary runs to four pages and mentions the smell twice. The newsletter mentions it in the first sentence and does not stop.

texts.title: The Case for the Slower Route
texts.author: Manuel Academy
texts.source: Authored for Manuel Academy High School ELA; Academy-held rights.
texts.summary: A sustained argument written for a named external audience, with an explicitly fair counterclaim.
texts.opening_passage: The fastest route is not in dispute. What is in dispute is whether speed is the thing this road is for.

texts.title: How a Correction Travels
texts.author: Manuel Academy
texts.source: Authored for Manuel Academy High School ELA; Academy-held rights.
texts.summary: Publication-quality explanatory model tracing how a factual correction propagates - and fails to - across formats.
texts.opening_passage: A correction is not the opposite of an error. It is a much slower, much quieter document that must travel the same distance the error already covered.
